scope: Manual correctness smokes for TypeScript legacy decorators and unsupported standard decorators across Quench HMR's TS/JS source paths; not a full TypeScript checker or decorators compatibility claim.

options: Read experimentalDecorators, emitDecoratorMetadata, strictNullChecks, and strict from resolved tsconfig.json.
Inline OXC's generated decorate, decorateMetadata, and decorateParam helpers in the prepared module while preserving generated source offsets before the appended helper declarations.
Use OXC AST validation on raw JavaScript and transformed JSX/TypeScript paths to reject standard decorators until the pinned transformer can lower them.
No @oxc-project/runtime installation is required by the application.

cases.scenario: Atomically replace a self-accepted decorated TypeScript entry while quench-node --hmr is running.
observed: Generation 1 decorator ran and global generation became 1.
Generation 2 decorator ran after the accepted replacement and global generation became 2.
The same quench-node CLI process remained running throughout the update.

cases.scenario: A TypeScript file uses standard decorators without experimentalDecorators.
observed: Quench exits with a clear unsupported-transform error from the pinned OXC transformer.
The previous behavior silently erased the decorator and ran the undecorated class; that behavior is no longer allowed.

cases.scenario: A JavaScript JSX file uses standard ECMAScript decorators.
observed: HMR exits with an explicit unsupported-transform error from the pinned OXC transformer.
Neither the decorator nor the module body runs, preventing silent loss of the decorator's behavior.

cases.scenario: Raw JavaScript entries and imported modules use standard ECMAScript decorators.
observed: All three entry formats exit with an explicit unsupported-transform error from the pinned OXC transformer.
Neither the decorator nor the module body runs.
The same rejection occurs for a CommonJS .cjs dependency and an ESM .mjs dependency before either importer body runs.
A plain .js control module executes normally with HMR enabled.

limits: A TSRS diagnostic from the ESM fixture installed 11 of 12 available parameter facts; this smoke does not qualify all queried types.

OXC 0.153.0 does not lower standard ECMAScript decorators. Quench rejects standard decorator syntax in raw JavaScript, JSX, and TypeScript modules; full standard decorator support remains unimplemented.
Only the listed legacy decorator forms and metadata were exercised, not all TypeScript compiler options or decorator edge cases.
Resident HMR control processes were terminated after observing output; decorator rejection cases exited with code 1 before module execution.
